intro2.text: Then you've come to a place with water and disagreements.

intro4.text: Good. Most applicants bring another disagreement.

workA.text: Everyone needs an accurate chart. Paying for one remains a minority interest. There's an old survey in that chest.

chestA.text: An old chart. Bring back my brass tankard from the window table and you can have the key.

fetchQ.text: Why don't you fetch the tankard?

fetchA.text: Because I have six customers' washing-up and one customer's ambition to encourage.

keepA.text: A chart ought to go somewhere. That one has mostly been under a blanket.

markersQ.text: The markers don't agree with it.

markersA.text: Then check which one has changed. Old doesn't always mean wrong.

makerQ.text: Do you know who made it?

makerA.text: People who knew this harbour before it acquired an advertising budget.

returnMug.text: My tankard! Here, take the chest key. The chart inside deserves some fresh air.

pickMug.text: One tankard acquired. My career in piracy begins modestly.

locked.text: Locked. Perhaps Mara knows where the key is.

chartFound.text: A chart to Bellweather Shoal! Finally, a plan with a suspicious dotted line.

chartDetail.text: These aren't decorative arrows. Someone measured the ebb channel.

chartQuestion.text: But the new marker outside points across it. Either this chart has aged badly, or somebody's improved the water.

keyHook.text: The key can stay on its hook. One less mystery in my pockets.

noMug.text: The tankard is already taken care of.

heavy.text: Too heavy. I'd have to chart a route just to lift it.

noBurn.text: A dramatic edit. I'll try a pencil first.

generic.text: An inspired combination. Unfortunately, the universe disagrees.

leaveIt.text: Best leave that where it is.

inanimate.text: It is keeping its thoughts to itself.

mugLook.text: A fine brass tankard. Someone has engraved property of Mara underneath.

chestLook.text: A sturdy sea chest. Its lock has survived more voyages than I have.

noticeLook.text: Shoreline observations wanted. Payment on verification. Below that: ship's cook wanted. Must distinguish salt from gunpowder.

windowLook.text: A warehouse corner, a lighthouse, and some very new buoys. Out there: a thousand possible adventures. In here: better heating.

fireLook.text: The only member of this establishment with a reliable work ethic.

maraLook.text: Mara runs a tight ship. Particularly impressive for a building.

orinLook.text: A navigator who has misplaced his ship. Promising.

lostA.text: I haven't lost my ship. I know exactly which ocean it's in.

lastQ.text: Where did you last see it?

lastA.text: At the berth indicated by an entirely official marker. It was a very reassuring marker.

readA.text: Bellweather Shoal. And the old transit marks. Match those from the outer landing before you trust either set of buoys.

transitA.text: Two fixed marks. Line them up and you know where you're looking. Much less opinionated than a sailor.

flowQ.text: Which way should the water run?

flowA.text: Depends on the tide and the channel. Use the board at the landing. Don't mistake one swirl for a conspiracy.

comeA.text: Find out whether the bridge is admitting pedestrians today. I'll keep an eye on the water from here.

eggLook.text: A work request headed Space Quest. One shelf. Six inches wider. Please. The bucket's been drawn as a rocket.

egg3.text: Mission accomplished. No worlds saved. Considerably less tripping.

egg4.text: That's how most useful jobs end.

eggRepeat.text: Still six inches. Still a frontier.

bridgeEntry.text: Halt! Captain Quibble owns this bridge. Passage costs three bruises to my ego.

rulesA.text: Five exchanges. Win three and you cross. Nobody gets hurt. Take your time; I have a very small jurisdiction.

swordA.text: There's a practice blade on that peg. Blunt as an unpaid compliment. We provide all necessary equipment.

publicQ.text: This plaque says the bridge is public.

publicA.text: And the public has been very careless about defending it.

companyA.text: Apparently my toll is an unauthorised obstruction. Their toll is infrastructure.

bye.text: I'll let you get back to it.

parrotLook.text: A parrot with a ledger. Nature's warning against teaching birds arithmetic.

quibbleLook.text: He has enough reputation for a fleet, and just enough bridge for himself.

signLook.text: One glorious victory. Exact change appreciated. Behind it: Fair Passage Company, harbour access agreements under review.

plaqueLook.text: For the use of the harbour. I suppose the captain is technically using it.

swordLook.text: A practice blade, thoughtfully blunted. Only pride gets hurt here.

ledgerLook.text: Expenses: ink, crackers, ink-flavoured crackers. These accounts are private, unlike this allegedly public bridge.

coda1.text: You've won. I still insist on the last word.

coda2.text: Then make it welcome. You keep the word. I keep walking.

coda3.text: Welcome. Hm. That was almost civilised.

post1.text: A temporary victory. The company's notice says it may replace all existing passage arrangements.

post3.text: Especially mine. It uses the word all in a most aggressive manner.

passed.text: The bridge is open to you. My dignity remains under repair.

landingEntry.text: An old survey, a new sign, and a harbour full of opinions. Time to make an observation.

boardLook.text: The tide board says ebb. Its diagram shows the usual flow in this channel going left. The new company arrow points right.

marksLook.text: Warehouse corner. Lighthouse notch. Fixed marks, unlike those floating buoys.

cleatLook.text: Stand here. Align warehouse corner with lighthouse notch. Finally, instructions that don't demand a subscription.

floatSnag.text: A current indicator, caught on that bolt. It tells me nothing while it's stuck.

floatFree.text: Free of the bolt, still safely tethered. Now the water can speak for itself.

hookLook.text: A public boathook. Return to rack. A refreshingly uncomplicated contract.

hookSelect.text: I can lift that snag with the boathook.

pullFloat.text: Pulling tightens the snag. I need to lift it with the boathook.

floatTake.text: This works better when it stays in the water.

paperFloat.text: Paper is an excellent current indicator exactly once.

buoyLook.text: A brass company signal buoy. Too far to reach. Close enough to watch.

boatLook.text: The monkey emblem of the Fair Passage Company. Their launch seems to know exactly where it's going.

needChart.text: I need the old chart from Mara's chest before I can make that comparison.

needBoard.text: I should read the tide board first. A direction without a tide phase isn't much of an argument.

needMarks.text: I should identify the fixed marks first. The warehouse corner and lighthouse notch look promising.

wrongMark.text: That's a floating marker. If it drifts, my whole argument drifts with it.

comparison1.text: The buildings haven't moved. Reassuring, if you're a building.

comparison2.text: This is the right channel. Now let's see whether the water agrees with the sign.

needCompare.text: First I need to compare the chart at the sighting cleat.

needFloat.text: The float is still snagged. I need a working indicator before I watch the channel.

observe0.text: Ebb tide. The float settles to the left, just as the board predicts.

observe1.text: Three amber flashes. Three bell strokes. That's a deliberate signal.

observe2.text: Now the float has swung right. Those leaves are going with it. The board still says ebb.

observe3.text: And the company launch enters immediately, following the new arrow.

conclusion1.text: A current can surprise a chart. That's why people like me get work.

conclusion2.text: But the bell knew first. And that boat was ready. Someone knows something the rest of the harbour doesn't.

wrongEvidence.text: I have observed one channel, not interviewed an ocean. Let's keep to what I actually saw.

evidenceDone.text: The change was local and coordinated with company traffic. Find out who operates the signals and whether this has happened before.

leadPip.text: If the harbour's doing tricks, somebody has already written a terrible headline.

leadHardware.text: Someone built that signal. Someone may remember how it's meant to work.

leadOrin.text: An official marker sent Orin to the wrong berth. I'd like to see which one.

end.text: I came looking for a job. I appear to have found a question. Tomorrow, I'll find out who else is asking it.

returnQ.text: A company boat knew when the current would turn.

returnMara.text: Then write down what you saw. People argue less successfully with a date and a drawing.

returnOrin.text: Then start with the signal, not with my reputation. One of those can still be repaired cheaply.

returnQuibble.text: Of course. Their signs are larger. Are we investigating that, or something worse?

returnParrot.text: The company wants me to sign its agreement before asking that question.

notYet.text: I should finish this observation before chasing another lead.
